Definition: neuter of a derivative of G5228; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story:--upper chamber (room).
BiblicalUsage: hyperōion means an upper room, an upper chamber. In Acts 1:13, the text says "they went up into an upper room." In Acts 9:37, the text says "they laid [her] in an upper chamber."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hyperōion matters because fellowship is sharing life together under Christ, not just sharing a room. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Conversion of Paul; Peter Raises Tabitha; Eutychus Raised at Troas
